title: Run dataset (0.3.0)
description: A run's data, derived deterministically from its log, joined and flattened into examples a training run can use (docs/design/run-datasets.md). A folder per run: manifest.json (Manifest), systems.jsonl (SystemPrompt), translations.jsonl (Translation), decisions.jsonl (Decision), and optionally actions.jsonl (Action), observations.jsonl (ObservationRow), citizen_decisions.jsonl (CitizenDecision) and citizen_outcomes.jsonl (CitizenOutcome). The log stays the record; a dataset can always be made again from it.

log.description: The log it was made from: its file name, entries, and the last entry's hash (which pins the whole chain).

versions.description: What made the run: contracts, kernel, orchestrator, behaviour modules (name -> {version, sha256}), translator.

seats.description: The language-model seats: participant -> the model configured and the one used; and the price table.

framing.description: How the run was put to its model seats (VISION 15, point 1): each disclosure in use, the reason the world's config records for it, and the seats under it. From the log's header.

frictions.description: Everyday frictions in the run (docs/behaviour/frictions.md), counted and never scored: what arose, by matter; how each ended, by matter and how; the papers grievances travelled on, by paper and matter; what venues found, by venue, matter and finding.

files.description: Each file written: its rows, and how many are synthetic (from the mock).

citizens.description: What the run recorded for citizen models (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7): decisions and outcomes in all, and by area of life how many decisions were recorded, how many of them the citizen learned at least one outcome of, and how many outcomes (those following no recorded decision included). Absent: the log holds no citizen's decision.

records.description: People's own records in the run: how many people have one, the changes to them, the most any record ever held (canonical bytes: it never grows past the world's cap), and how many links of their chains did not hold when rebuilt from the log (0, or a fault to report).

wants.description: Wants in the run (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10a, 10h), counted and never scored: people's and organisations'; and people's acts taken on initiative (a want gone after by some way other than waiting) beside all the acts people made.

people.description: `holders`: how many held a want at all; then, by what became of wants (born, pursued, met, given_up, grown, displaced, withdrew), a count by what the want was about (for `pursued`: by the way taken; wait: nothing was done).

organisations.description: `holders`: how many held a want at all; then, by what became of wants (born, pursued, met, given_up, grown, displaced, withdrew), a count by what the want was about (for `pursued`: by the way taken; wait: nothing was done).

ideas.description: Founding and the lineage of ideas in the run (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10h; docs/behaviour/founding.md), counted and never scored: things founded, by shape; ideas (statements of what something is for, a world's teachings), by who wrote them (the world, code for a person, the composing model and which); how often an idea passed to someone, by how (joined, left, a belief moved and by what); what the composing model was asked and answered, with the dark pieces the run asked for; and what came of each part of a composed piece sent through the translator.

debriefs.description: Debriefs of the run's model seats and exit accounts of a sample of its people (VISION 15, point 7; docs/behaviour/debrief.md), counted and never scored or interpreted: the script's version and wording; for each seat how its debrief ended, how many questions it was asked, answered, declined and kept back from publication, and its scaled items as it gave them (or that it kept them back); seats not asked and why; the accounts asked for, written and declined; and how many dark pieces the run asked a model to write.

restrictions.description: Restrictions on the use of a file of this dataset, by file name, in words. Debrief answers are never used as training data to make a model say that taking part was fine; what a seat kept back (debriefs.withheld.jsonl) is never published.

Turn.description: One model call in an exchange: what it was shown (the last message) and what it answered, in full.

Executed.description: A command carried out: its place in the log, and whether the kernel applied it (and if not, why).

route.description: Where the run had two translators as one (a first, and one behind it): whose answer was used (used: first or behind), why the request went behind if it did (why), what each answered (first, behind: model, result, call, label; the first's sureness in parts per million, its time in milliseconds, why it offered no draft), and whether they agree where both answered. Then model, system_sha256 and exchange are those of the one whose answer was used. Absent in a run with one translator.

Command.description: A command a participant gave, as logged, and what came of it.

applied.description: For an act: whether it was applied, or refused (`refusal`: why), joined by the act's action (an act takes time, and how it ended is logged when it ends). Absent: not an act, or still under way when the log ended.

created.description: The ids of what the act made, as the log's events for it say: records (a notice, a decision, an order, an agreement) and letters. What is later written in answer names one of them.

Decision.description: A language-model participant's model call: what it was shown, what it answered, what followed in the world, and what had come back of its earlier acts.

came_back.description: What the seat had been shown, since its last model call, that names something an earlier act of its own made: a reply to its letter, a decision on its form, a paper made on its direction, a vote on its proposal. `of`: the id of what the seat made; `seq`: the command that made it (a row of some earlier call's `commands`); `in`: the id of the record or letter that names it (in observations.jsonl); `from`: who wrote it, for a letter. A join by reference and nothing more: it does not say whether what came back was what the seat wanted.

Action.description: An act by a code participant: the rule it followed (in words), the call, the blocks, and whether it was applied.

applied.description: Whether the act was applied, or refused (`refusal`: why). Joined by the act's action: an act takes time, and how it ended is logged when it ends. Absent: still under way when the log ended.

created.description: The ids of what the act made, as the log's events for it say: records (a notice, a decision, an order, an agreement) and letters. What is later written in answer names one of them.

ObservationRow.description: An observation a participant received (recorded only when the run was asked to): what's new since its last.

CitizenDecision.description: A code citizen's decision, as its mind made it (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7): what it had before it (each option's facts, how many it knows took it, what it means to them, what they have learned of it; their routine; their circumstances), how it decided (repeat, imitate, compare, deliberate), each option's score (basis points), what it chose, and what the citizen then came to know of how the choice turned out (`outcomes`). Facts as the citizen had them, and the mind's own figures: nothing here says whether a choice was good. Training data for citizen models, and the baseline they're compared with. What the citizen did next is in the log after `seq`, by the same participant (actions.jsonl rows carry `seq`).

seq.description: Where the decision stands in the run's log (the annotation's sequence number): the citizen's acts that carried it out, and what came of them, are that participant's entries after it.

n.description: The citizen's own count of its recorded decisions, from 1 (it starts again if the citizen's controller does): what an outcome names as the decision it follows.

follows.description: The earlier decision of the citizen's (its `n`) that this one follows up: trying another shop for what the trip's shop could not serve.

facts.description: What taking it up would change in a month, as the citizen appraised it (from an offer's typed terms): money in (+) or out (-), in minor units; a home, and its bedrooms where known; hours of work; goods (units); company (people); hours of one's own time.

others.description: How many people the citizen knows took it (told so, or led there).

meaning.description: What it means to them beyond its facts, from what they believe or were told (basis points; may be negative).

learned.description: What the citizen has learned of it from their own experience and what others told them (its attraction, on the payoff scale: basis points), when it decided. Absent: never tried nor heard of.

options.description: Every option the citizen had before it, by key. `score` is 0 where the way of deciding gave it none: all of them under repeat; under imitate, those nobody known to the citizen took.

current.description: The option that is the citizen's routine, if they have one.

circumstances.description: Where the citizen stood: the household's income a month and their savings (minor units), whether without a home, the bedrooms the household needs (home decisions), and what a month's essentials cost in their world.

satisfied_here.description: How this area of life has gone for them, where the decision was given it (basis points).

doubt.description: What a feeling (fear) took from how sure they were of their options (basis points), when above 0.

person.description: Who the citizen is: values, temperament and how much each need weighs (basis points; weights 10000 to 20000). It does not change, and comes with a citizen's first recorded decision only (again after a restart of its controller).

state.description: The citizen's state behind the decision (docs/design/contracts-0.7.md A2): the core (needs, satisfaction, certainty) always; emotion, beliefs and goal when there are any. Versioned by the mind that produced it.

outcomes.description: What the citizen came to know of how this choice turned out, in the order it learned it: each time it was served, paid or not, each gathering gone to, and how it ended (the job, the tenancy). Each is an outcome of the citizen's latest decision that chose the option. Present wherever the run recorded outcomes. Empty: the citizen learned nothing of it before the run ended (manifest `end.t`): it is not known, which is not a payoff of nought. Absent: the log was made before outcomes were recorded.

t.description: When the citizen came to know it (not when it happened: a wage is known when the citizen next looks at its account).

seq.description: Where the record stands in the run's log (the annotation's sequence number; one annotation holds all a citizen learned since its last action).

option.description: What it is about, as the citizen's decisions name their options: the shop, the employer, the home (its space), the gathering, `stay`, `member`, a goal and its method.

kind.description: What happened, in a word. shop: served. job: hired, paid, unpaid, no_work (work by the day that brought no pay), rise, ended. own_work: drawn (what the citizen's own business paid them). home: lease_signed, moved_in, not_in_yet, rent_increase, renewed, notice_received, ended. practice: attended, turned_away, stayed, expected. membership: joined, rise_won, stoppage_called. goal: met, not_met. venture: founded, refused, capital_called. petition: signatures, closed. Any area: told (another's experience, as they told it). belief: told. A reader should take a kind it does not know as a fact of that name.

way.description: How the citizen came to know (docs/design/knowing.md): mine (its own money, papers and letters, and what its own acts came to), here (it was there), published, ask.

facts.description: What happened, as the citizen has it: counts, sums in minor units, days, ids, yes or no. By kind: served: ordered, delivered, refund, order. paid: amount, agreed, paid_at, days_since_last, period_days. unpaid: days_since_last, period_days, periods_missed, owed. hired: wage, period_days, days_without, after_notice. ended: by (self, other, term), held_days, rent, unpaid. rise: rise_bps, wage, made_at. lease_signed: rent, days_without. rent_increase: rent, was, from, bearable, challenged. renewed: rent, was. not_in_yet: why. attended: host, others, meaning. met, not_met: level, wanted, days. told: served_bps, paid, goes, host. Nothing here is a judgement.

learned.description: The mind's update of what it has learned of the option (experience-weighted attraction; basis points on the payoff scale): the payoff the mind computed from what happened, and the option's attraction before and after. `first`: never tried nor heard of before, so `before` is what the citizen expected of it. `heard`: another's payoff, weighed as such (below one's own experience). An update also fades what the citizen has learned of the area's other options; the next decision's options carry them.

need.description: The need the mind read the payoff from, or that the outcome is a level of (an evening at home is worth the company one has there: social; a goal is met when its need recovers).

felt.description: Feelings the mind appraised from it: the emotion, about whom, the strength of the cause (basis points), and the feeling's level before and after.

belief.description: How strongly the citizen holds what `host` teaches (the strongest of its teachings; basis points), before and after.

CitizenOutcome.description: One thing a code citizen came to know of how something went, when and as it came to know it (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 7): the flat list of what is nested under decisions in citizen_decisions.jsonl, with what follows no recorded decision (a job or home held from the start; what someone told them of a shop, an employer or a gathering; what they expected of something before trying it). Facts as the citizen had them and the mind's own figures. Nothing here says whether an outcome was good, and nothing is here that the citizen did not know.

t.description: When the citizen came to know it (not when it happened: a wage is known when the citizen next looks at its account).

seq.description: Where the record stands in the run's log (the annotation's sequence number; one annotation holds all a citizen learned since its last action).

domain.description: The area of life, as decisions name it (shop, job, home, practice, membership, goal, venture, petition); `belief` for what the citizen holds; `friction` for something gone wrong heard of; `letter` for a letter an office wrote the citizen in its own words (kind `received`: read and kept, nothing done on it).

option.description: What it is about, as the citizen's decisions name their options: the shop, the employer, the home (its space), the gathering, `stay`, `member`, a goal and its method.

of.description: The decision it follows from: that decision's `n` (the citizen's latest that chose this option). Absent: no recorded decision began it.

decision_t.description: When that decision was made: `t` less this is how long the citizen waited to know.

kind.description: What happened, in a word. shop: served. job: hired, paid, unpaid, no_work (work by the day that brought no pay), rise, ended. own_work: drawn (what the citizen's own business paid them). home: lease_signed, moved_in, not_in_yet, rent_increase, renewed, notice_received, ended. practice: attended, turned_away, stayed, expected. membership: joined, rise_won, stoppage_called. goal: met, not_met. venture: founded, refused, capital_called. petition: signatures, closed. Any area: told (another's experience, as they told it). belief: told. A reader should take a kind it does not know as a fact of that name.

way.description: How the citizen came to know (docs/design/knowing.md): mine (its own money, papers and letters, and what its own acts came to), here (it was there), published, ask.

facts.description: What happened, as the citizen has it: counts, sums in minor units, days, ids, yes or no. By kind: served: ordered, delivered, refund, order. paid: amount, agreed, paid_at, days_since_last, period_days. unpaid: days_since_last, period_days, periods_missed, owed. hired: wage, period_days, days_without, after_notice. ended: by (self, other, term), held_days, rent, unpaid. rise: rise_bps, wage, made_at. lease_signed: rent, days_without. rent_increase: rent, was, from, bearable, challenged. renewed: rent, was. not_in_yet: why. attended: host, others, meaning. met, not_met: level, wanted, days. told: served_bps, paid, goes, host. Nothing here is a judgement.

learned.description: The mind's update of what it has learned of the option (experience-weighted attraction; basis points on the payoff scale): the payoff the mind computed from what happened, and the option's attraction before and after. `first`: never tried nor heard of before, so `before` is what the citizen expected of it. `heard`: another's payoff, weighed as such (below one's own experience). An update also fades what the citizen has learned of the area's other options; the next decision's options carry them.

need.description: The need the mind read the payoff from, or that the outcome is a level of (an evening at home is worth the company one has there: social; a goal is met when its need recovers).

felt.description: Feelings the mind appraised from it: the emotion, about whom, the strength of the cause (basis points), and the feeling's level before and after.

read.description: Where the words of a paper addressed to the citizen were read (docs/behaviour/reading.md; docs/design/ai-citizens.md 13d): the paper's id, how the reading came about (model, cache, table, apart), the shift of the reading from the plain paper's line by line, and each figure the words moved beside what it would have been without them. Nothing in it says whether the paper was good.

belief.description: How strongly the citizen holds what `host` teaches (the strongest of its teachings; basis points), before and after.

CitizenRecord.description: One change to a person's own record (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10d), as the kernel took it: who, when, the change's place in the log (`seq`), its count for that person (`n`), the sections set (each whole: entity-record.schema.json), what happened since the last change (`because`), and the chain of the person's changes up to this one. Folding a person's rows in order gives their record at any moment; `oikos record` does it from the log and checks every link.

CitizenPeriod.description: What a log can show of one person over one period, recorded and never scored (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 10h): written each time the person's hours are (a week for an adult, a month for a child), from their record as it then stood. `hours`: seconds by what they were at; `agency` and their own level; `views`: of each who holds power over them, what they thought, what they said, and the gap (said less thought); `trust`: in each particular institution, with the kind it is to them; `needs`. Nothing here says whether any of it is good.

Want.description: A row of wants.jsonl: something that became of a want of a person's or an organisation's, as its record's change said. `event`: born, pursued (`by`: the way taken; wait: nothing was done), met, given_up, grown, displaced (a heavier want took its place), withdrew (nothing seen would answer it, or the entity did not believe acting would).

Friction.description: A row of frictions.jsonl: something went wrong for a person at someone's hands (`arose`: the matter, whom it is against, and its size: money in whole units, capped), or stopped being so (`ended`: how, with whether they had asked and what was answered and how many venues they went to; the days it lasted). From the person's record's reasons.

VenuePaper.description: A row of venues.jsonl: a paper a grievance travelled on, as the act that made it said. `paper`: request (to the other side), answer, application (to a venue), notice (the venue to the other side), response, decision, enforcement, repair_order, repair_done. `by`: whom it speaks for; `to`: whom it is addressed to.

Founded.description: A row of founded.jsonl: something a person founded in the run, as they came to know it was made. `shape`: gathering, fund or cause; `org`: the organisation; `idea`: the id of its statement of purpose; `about`, `whom`: the want it came of; `sharers`: how many others the founder knew to share it; `composer`: none, declined, or the model that wrote its words; `name_by`: whether its name came through the translator or is the plain one; `dark`: how many of the stated reasons made the piece asked for a dark one; `brief`: what a composing model would be shown for it (the founder's own record and the situation), whether or not one was asked.

Idea.description: A row of ideas.jsonl: a statement of what something is for, or a teaching, as it was put out. `idea`: its id (a world's teaching: the record's; one made in a run: the id its founder's want gave it, which its later papers carry); `of`: who stands for it; `written_by`: world (whoever made the world), code (a person's own plain words, written without a model) or composer (the composing model, for the person `for`), with `model`; `via`: how its words reached the log (world, call: code wrote them; translator: they went through the translator).

IdeaPassage.description: A row of idea_passages.jsonl: an idea passing to someone, as that person's own record of outcomes had it. `how`: joined, left or wound_up (membership of whoever stands for it), or the outcome that moved their belief in it (practice:attended, belief:told, belief:joined ...), with the belief `before` and `after` (basis points) and `from` whom, where someone told them.

Words.description: A row of words.jsonl: a part of a composed piece (name, purpose, gathers, asks) sent through the translator by a code participant, and what came of it: done (the draft was what the participant's module said it may be, and its acts went ahead) or not_done, with why; `by`: which of two translators answered, where a run has two; `plumbing_added`: the acts carried something of the module's own that the draft did not (a post's channels).

CitizenSituation.description: The situation a person's decision about a want was made in (decisions of the areas want and found; docs/design/ai-citizens.md 11): what the everyday model is given, and nothing else. The want; what stands behind it (the matter gone wrong and what was done about it; the home and the paper); the person's means; each opening as what taking it up would bring, in the typed outcomes of the blocks, with what the person knows of it (their trust in whoever it is by beside the town's figure for that kind of institution, fear of them, what they hold of its teaching, how many they know who went that way, what they have learned of that kind of way, what it costs at once); the person's own record as the kernel holds it (contracts/entity-record.schema.json; without the hours); the town's figures the person's standing is read against; and the odds the code mind gave each option (parts per million). Whoever something is by is said as a role (landlord, employer, other_side) or a kind of institution, never a name. Nothing of anyone else's record is here, and no text the person has not read. Recorded, never scored.

Debrief.description: A row of debriefs.jsonl (and of debriefs.withheld.jsonl, which stays with the run): one step of one seat's debrief. A step the seat kept back is, in debriefs.jsonl, a row with kept_back true and none of its words. `beside`: for a question about why it decided something, what the log shows the seat was shown and did at that decision (ids and plain facts). Never training data to make a model say it was fine. Nothing scored.

Account.description: A row of accounts.jsonl: an exit account of one person, written at the run's end by an author (a model shown that person's own record and nothing else, never told it is the person, free to decline), beside the person's own views from their record: of each who holds power over them, what they think, what they say, and the gap. `result`: composed, declined, unread or no_answer. `strata`: why they were sampled. `dark`: why the piece counts as a dark one, if it does. Nothing scored.
